t: Between 230 and 221 BCE King Zheng of Qin conquered Han, Zhao, Yan, Wei, Chu and Qi, ending the Warring States period, and took the new title of huangdi, which Chinese monarchs used for the next two millennia.

With his minister Li Si he replaced the feudal order with commanderies and counties and standardised weights, measures, coinage and script, while mobilising hundreds of thousands of workers for walls, roads, canals and his tomb.

Traditional historiography portrayed him as a brutal tyrant who burned books and buried scholars alive; scholars since the mid-20th century have questioned that picture, which stems partly from the Han dynasty that replaced the Qin.
dyk: After the emperor died on tour, the chancellor Li Si hid the death for the two months' journey back to the capital, ordering carts of rotten fish to travel before and behind the imperial wagon to cover the smell of the body.
ev: Zheng is born in Handan, the capital of Zhao, where his father, the Qin prince Yiren, lives as a hostage
He succeeds his father King Zhuangxiang as king of Qin at the age of 13, with Lü Buwei as regent prime minister
Lao Ai seizes the queen mother's seal and attempts a coup; he is torn to pieces and his family executed to the third degree
Jing Ke, sent by Crown Prince Dan of Yan, tries to stab the king with a dagger hidden in a map and fails
Qin armies capture King Jian of Qi, completing the unification, and Zheng proclaims himself the First Emperor
General Meng Tian routs the Xiongnu from the Ordos Plateau on the emperor's orders
At the instigation of Li Si the emperor orders most existing books to be burned
He dies at Shaqiu on his fifth eastern tour; a forged letter brings his younger son Huhai to the throne as the Second Emperor

f.born: February 259 BCE in Handan, capital of the state of Zhao; son of the Qin prince Yiren, later King Zhuangxiang of Qin, and Lady Zhao
f.died: July or August 210 BCE, at the palace in Shaqiu prefecture during his fifth tour of eastern China, aged 49; the cause is unknown
f.role: King Zheng of Qin (from 246 BCE, with full power from 235 BCE); First Emperor, Shi Huangdi (221–210 BCE), founder of the Qin dynasty
f.known: unifying China in 221 BCE; creating the title huangdi, emperor; standardising weights, measures, coinage, axle lengths and script; commanderies and counties in place of the feudal system; the northern walls that preceded the Great Wall; the burning of books; his mausoleum and the Terracotta Army; the search for an elixir of life
